column1: # Eval corpus: real fix-commits from a private repo (szarkans/pshk-bot).
# Each case checks out the repo AT the fix, then reverts the fix in source
# files only — so the working tree contains the bug and the diff under review
# is "the bug being introduced". Tests and docs stay at the fixed state and are
# fields: id <TAB> fix-commit <TAB> source paths to revert <TAB> ground truth

column4: Loyalty add/gift is a non-atomic read-modify-write: no row lock is taken before the anti-replay check and the mutation, so two concurrent scans of the same QR both pass and double-stamp the user.

RSVP accepts an event_id that does not exist or was soft-deleted (no existence check), and two concurrent first RSVPs both insert, so the loser crashes with an unhandled IntegrityError instead of returning the winner's state.
Concurrent first-time registration of the same telegram_id races: both requests miss the existing row and the loser's commit raises an unhandled IntegrityError.
Broadcast accepts an empty caption/text and sends a blank message to everyone; user-supplied names and text are interpolated into HTML-parse-mode messages without escaping.

The preview-card send loses its TelegramBadRequest fallback in _send_card: when answer_photo is rejected, the error propagates instead of sending the text card, so admins with bad media get a crash instead of the fallback text. Publish status itself is not affected.
